title: Purify Plus opens again, and highlights learn to look like ink
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This patch mends the most serious kind of bug we can ship: tapping Purify Plus closed the app outright. The fault was two billing components speaking different versions of the same language deep in the Android layer, and it is fixed at the root. While we were in the reader we also freed anyone the app had trapped in focus mode, and gave highlights the look they always deserved: ink on the words, not a bar in the margin. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Purify Plus opens again
sections.body: Tapping Purify Plus crashed the app the moment the subscription screen tried to wake the billing machinery. Two of its components had drifted onto incompatible versions, and the collision brought the whole app down. They now move in lockstep, and the paywall opens, prices load from Google Play, and Restore works as intended. If Plus ever cannot load, you will see a calm explanation instead of a crash.

sections.heading: A guaranteed way out of focus mode
sections.body: Focus reading hides the app around the text. A recent restructuring accidentally left the top bar standing invisible over the Exit button, swallowing every tap, and on a phone there is no Escape key to fall back on. The exit now floats above everything by construction, the app chrome truly steps aside, and a new automated test presses the real button on every build so this cannot quietly return.

sections.heading: Highlights look like ink now
sections.body: A highlighted verse used to wear a plain colored bar down its left margin. It now carries a quiet wash of its color across the words themselves, line by line, the way a real highlighter moves. Word-level highlights stay brighter inside it, and the writings of the saints receive the same treatment in gold.

closing: The Plus crash was reported by a reader and reproduced within the hour. If anything else misbehaves, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: One hand for every symbol, and two checkout bugs caught live
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. Two kinds of work in this patch. First, we walked the live shop the way a customer would and caught two real bugs at the door: a product page that could sit loading forever, and a checkout that returned buyers to a dead page after paying or backing out. Both are fixed and the whole cancel path is now verified against live Stripe. Second, every symbol in the app's buttons and controls now comes from one hand: our own icon family, drawn on one grid with one stroke, replacing the mismatched keyboard characters and third-party glyphs that had crept in. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Checkout, walked and mended
sections.body: Backing out of a live payment used to strand you on a broken page, and the same flaw would have caught paying customers after checkout. Return addresses now always point home. We also proved the abandon path end to end against live Stripe: leave the payment page and the attempt cancels itself, with nothing charged and nothing lingering in your orders.

sections.heading: Pages that never say almost
sections.body: A product page could hang on its loading bones if the app was waiting on a stale sign-in check held by another tab. Pages now refuse to wait on niceties: the shipping perk check gives itself a short deadline and steps aside, and the page simply loads.

sections.heading: The webhook grew armor
sections.body: The machinery that marks orders paid now verifies the charged amount against the order before believing anything, and if a payment lands on an order that was cancelled a heartbeat earlier, the payment wins and the order is restored. Eleven new tests hold these rules in place.

sections.heading: One family of symbols
sections.body: The bookmark star, the note pen, the copy link, the highlight spark, the cart plus and minus, the close cross, the menu lines, the rating stars, the save heart: all now drawn in Purify's own hand, on one grid, with one stroke, crisp in every button on every screen. The link symbol no longer turns into a colored emoji on Android, and the same action now wears the same symbol everywhere it appears.

sections.heading: A clearer footing on the bottom bar
sections.body: The selected tab now speaks three ways: its color, its sliding backdrop, and a slightly firmer line in the icon itself, so the active tab reads clearly without leaning on color alone.

closing: Found by walking the aisles ourselves, mended the same afternoon. If anything else is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The shop, refined: a cart, honest orders, and a smoother checkout
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. The shop opened its doors inside the app this morning, and the first walkers-through found the loose boards by evening. This patch mends every one of them and adds the piece most shops are born with: a cart. Icons pages no longer error on desktop, walking away from checkout no longer leaves a ghost in your orders, and paying for an icon now ends with a moment worthy of the purchase. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: A cart, at last
sections.body: Every icon page now carries Add to cart beside Buy now. The cart lives on your device, shows a running count on its tab, lets you adjust quantities, and checks out everything in one payment with one shipping charge. Purify Plus members still ship free on every order.

sections.heading: Orders that tell the truth
sections.body: Starting a checkout and then walking away used to leave a phantom order marked as confirmed. No more. Backing out of the payment page cancels the attempt on the spot, unfinished checkouts appear only as a quiet removable note, never among your real orders, and anything unpaid says plainly: Awaiting Payment.

sections.heading: Icon pages on desktop, mended
sections.body: Opening an icon or the EIKON storefront on the desktop website could answer with an internal server error. The root cause is fixed and every shop page opens cleanly on every screen.

sections.heading: A proper amen to your payment
sections.body: When your payment goes through, a gold ring now draws its check, and the confirmation rises beneath it. Small, quick, and honored if your device asks for reduced motion.

sections.heading: Faster, calmer surfaces
sections.body: Shop pages now load with quiet placeholder cards instead of a bare loading line, browsing back and forth is instant, messages show who is speaking with the composer always in reach, and the browser tab reads cleanly on every shop page.

sections.heading: Account, always reachable
sections.body: On desktop, the account page could sit on a loading skeleton if the redirect script never woke. The skeleton now carries a plain link to your profile that works even with no script at all.

closing: Found within hours, mended within hours. If anything else is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The Fathers, doubled: the whole Psalter with Augustine
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This patch is one thing only, and it is a large thing: commentary. A reader on the Discord asked for more of the Fathers, enough to stand beside any catena Bible, and this is the answer. The library of patristic commentary in Purify roughly doubles today, to four thousand four hundred and eighty-one verse-notes across twenty-three books of Scripture, from fifteen Fathers of the Church. Every word of it is the Fathers' own, from named public-domain translations, and we tell you exactly which. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: The whole Psalter, with St. Augustine
sections.body: The crown of this patch. St. Augustine's Expositions on the Book of Psalms now stands beside every one of the hundred and fifty psalms, one thousand eight hundred and ninety-eight notes keyed verse by verse. Open any psalm, tap a red-dotted verse, and Augustine prays it with you. Because Purify's Psalter is the Septuagint and Augustine preached from it too, his psalm often meets yours word for word. From the Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers, volume eight.

sections.heading: The six days, with St. Basil
sections.body: St. Basil the Great's nine homilies of the Hexaemeron, the Church's great preaching on the days of creation, now stand in Genesis 1 in full, each homily set on the verse whose command it opens with. In the beginning God made the heaven and the earth; Basil takes it from there.

sections.heading: A second voice on the Gospel of John
sections.body: St. Augustine's one hundred and twenty-four Tractates on the Gospel of John now read alongside St. John Chrysostom's eighty-eight homilies, two Fathers on one Gospel, across all twenty-one chapters. Where they stand on the same verse, you read them together.

sections.heading: Revelation, opened
sections.body: The Apocalypse receives its first commentary in Purify: St. Victorinus of Pettau, bishop and martyr of the Diocletianic persecution, whose commentary on Revelation is the earliest that survives from the whole Church. Eighty-eight notes across nineteen chapters, from the Ante-Nicene Fathers, volume seven.

sections.heading: The first verse, reachable
sections.body: Commentary on a chapter's opening verse was hidden on phones: the illuminated drop cap left no room for the red marker, and the long-press menu pointed at a desktop-only panel. The opening verse now carries its marker after the text, and the menu opens the commentary sheet properly. Genesis 1:1, John 1:1, and every psalm's opening are reachable with a tap.

sections.heading: On languages, honestly
sections.body: The same reader asked for commentary in the app's other languages. The Fathers here are public-domain English translations, named on every note, and we will not run them through a machine and call it a translation. Faithful editions in other languages are future work, done properly or not at all.

closing: Asked for on the Discord, and answered with the biggest single addition of the Fathers Purify has ever shipped. If a note sits on the wrong verse or a word looks wrong, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com; every citation names its source so you can check us. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The shop comes inside
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. Until now the EIKON shop opened in your phone's browser, a door that led out of the app. This patch brings the whole shop inside: a Shop tab on the bottom bar, every icon browsable and buyable without leaving Purify or signing in again, checkout completed in the app, and your orders and your messages to the seller waiting when you return. And a first for EIKON: reviews you can trust, left only by people who actually bought the item, with a plain count of how many have sold. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: The shop, inside the app
sections.body: The marketplace now lives in Purify itself, not a browser window. A new Shop tab sits on the bottom bar beside Today, the Bible, Discover, and Prayers. Browse the icons, open a listing, read the details, and buy, all without leaving the app and without signing in a second time. Your orders and your conversations with the seller are there when you come back.

sections.heading: Checkout, without leaving
sections.body: Buying an icon now happens in the app. You tap Buy, the secure Stripe page opens over the app to take the card, and when it closes you land back on your orders, where the new order appears and moves from confirmed to shipped. Purify Plus members still ship free on every order.

sections.heading: Reviews you can trust
sections.body: Every icon and every store can now carry a star rating, and a review can be left only by someone who actually bought the item, so no rating is idle talk. Each listing shows its average stars, how many reviews it has, and a plain count of how many have sold. Where nothing has sold or been reviewed yet, nothing is shown; we would rather say little than pad it out.

sections.heading: Message the seller, reach your requests
sections.body: Now that the shop is inside the app, messaging the seller and tracking an Icon Request work from your pocket the same as on the web. Ask about an order, request a saint the catalog does not hold yet, and read the replies, all in one place.

closing: The shop was the last room of Purify that still opened outward; now every room is under one roof. If anything is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The account pages, mended
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. A quick repair patch for three crashes the first users found on the app: the account pages, the Purify Plus screen, and a top bar that slipped under the clock in the reader. All three are mended. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: Your account, reachable again
sections.body: On the app, opening Account and security, or Notifications, was bouncing you back to sign-in or closing the screen. The offline app checks who you are the wrong way on those pages; it now checks the right way, so your profile, security, notification, and session settings all open as they should, without signing you out.

sections.heading: Purify Plus opens cleanly
sections.body: The Purify Plus screen could close the app if the store took a moment to answer. It now opens to a calm screen every time, and never closes the app if billing is slow to load.

sections.heading: The top bar clears the clock
sections.body: In the Bible reader, the little book-and-verse strip at the top could slip up under the phone's clock and battery. It now sits clear of the status bar, in the reader and everywhere else the top bar appears.

closing: Small and quick, offered with thanks to everyone testing on day one. If anything else is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: Launch-day repairs, with thanks
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. The doors opened today, and the first walkers-through found the loose boards. This patch mends them the same day: Google sign-in on the Play build, an account step in the welcome flow, the Plus screen set right with the true mark of the app, the shop reachable from your phone, and a set of small collisions and rough edges smoothed. Thank you to everyone who wrote in within hours; this is what a launch day should look like.

sections.heading: Signing in, truly mended
sections.body: Google sign-in on the Play-installed app was failing at the last step and calling it a cancellation; the app's Play signing certificate was not fully registered on our side. It is registered now, and the app also tells the truth about what went wrong if anything like it ever recurs. Creating an account now signs you in immediately, no confirmation detour, and you stay signed in on that device. The welcome flow gained a fourth step: keep your journey with a Google or email account, entirely optional.

sections.heading: The Plus screen, set right
sections.body: The Purify Plus screen now wears the app's own mark, the white three-bar cross in the black circle, and the signed-out view no longer strands a lone button at the bottom of an empty screen: what Plus includes is laid out before the door asks for a key.

sections.heading: The shop, in your pocket
sections.body: Discover now carries the EIKON shop on phones. In the app it opens the storefront in your browser, where checkout lives; on the mobile site it is simply another door in the library.

sections.heading: Small collisions, smoothed
sections.body: The bookmark button no longer hides behind the Android status bar when you scroll. The book picker in the Bible is a proper bottom sheet on phones instead of a desktop popover. The saints index scrolls lighter on mid-range phones. And the About page now says plainly what has always been true: Purify is an Eastern Orthodox led project.

closing: A launch is a beginning, not a finish line. If anything else is loose, write to lifeistheosis@gmail.com and it will be mended with the same speed. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: The doors open: the EIKON shop, Purify Plus, and the Hours
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This patch opens two doors we have been building behind for a long season. The EIKON shop is open: hand-picked icons and prayer goods, each one inspected before it ships to you. And Purify Plus arrives on Android, the optional subscription that keeps the lamps lit, with cross-device sync, notes and highlights everywhere, and free shipping on everything in the shop. Alongside the doors, the prayer corner grows: the Little Hours now carry their Psalms in full, a rule of protection joins the devotional shelf, and the greatest born of women, St. John the Baptist, takes his place among the saints. The core of Purify stays free, today and always.

sections.heading: The EIKON shop is open
sections.body: A marketplace for the prayer corner at /shop, beginning with the EIKON store: icons, prayer ropes, censers, and the goods of a working prayer life. Every item is sourced, inspected by our own hands, and repackaged before it ships; every listing says plainly how it is made and where it comes from. Checkout is by card through Stripe, shipping within the United States, and the shipping and returns policy is written in plain words at /shop/policies. If an icon you love is missing, the Request an Icon door is open.

sections.heading: Purify Plus, on Android
sections.body: The optional subscription is live in the Android app: $9.99 a month or $99 a year, billed securely through Google Play, cancel anytime. Plus carries your library across devices, syncs your notes, highlights, and bookmarks, unlocks custom collections and the Florilegium, and ships everything in the EIKON shop free while your subscription is active. Buying it genuinely unlocks it: the entitlement is written server-side to your account the moment Google confirms the purchase, and Restore brings it back on any device you sign in on. What is free today stays free; Plus pays for the servers and the work, it never buys back what was given.

sections.heading: The Hours, in full
sections.body: The First, Third, Sixth, and Ninth Hours now carry their three appointed Psalms each in full, in Brenton's public-domain Septuagint translation, with the fixed troparion and dismissal of each hour. The Book of Hours was asked for on the Discord, with the psalm structure laid out carefully by the one who asked; here it is, and the Hours now stand in the daily rule beside Compline.

sections.heading: Prayers of protection, and the Forerunner
sections.body: A new rule of protection joins the devotional shelf: Psalm 90 and Psalm 26 in full, the Let God arise verses prayed with the sign of the Cross, and the petition for the guard of the angel, every word verbatim from public-domain sources. And St. John the Baptist, the Forerunner, of whom the Lord said that among them born of women there hath not risen a greater, takes his place among the saints with his whole scriptural witness, from the annunciation to Zacharias to the Beheading. Both were asked for on the Discord.

sections.heading: Repairs you asked for
sections.body: The calendar's New and Old toggle no longer sticks on Old for installed-app readers; the choice now holds everywhere. Focus mode releases you again on desktop, by the exit button or the Escape key. The buttons at the very top of the screen answer taps again on iPhone. And the Read the Gospel with Chrysostom door now tells you plainly how to open the commentary beside the text. Each of these came from a community report, named in the suggestions forum, and each is mended.

sections.heading: The small print, kept honest
sections.body: The Terms of Service now spell out the subscription plainly, the price, the renewal, and how to cancel, and the shop's shipping and returns policy stands at /shop/policies as part of them. Agreement is now a real checkbox at signup and at checkout, and your acceptance is recorded, because a promise should be provable on both sides. The privacy policy already names every processor involved: Stripe for the shop, Google Play and RevenueCat for Plus.

closing: Two doors and a fuller prayer corner. If an item arrives short of what you hoped, if a psalm reads wrong, or if Plus does not unlock what it promised, write to me at lifeistheosis@gmail.com and it will be made right. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: A walk through the history of the Church
intro: Welcome, and glory to Jesus Christ. This is the largest patch since Purify began, and the one I most wanted to build. The whole story of the Orthodox Church now lives in the app as an interactive timeline you can walk with your own hand: thirty-eight events across eleven ages, from the fire of Pentecost to the Church of our own day, each one sourced, cited, and honest about what is certain and what is held in loving tradition. Around it, the three pages you open most, Today, the Bible, and Discover, have been redrawn to feel like one quiet, considered whole. And Continue with Google, which had gone quiet, sings again. However you came to be here, new face or old friend, thank you for walking this history with us.

sections.heading: Orthodox History, an interactive timeline
sections.body: A new home under Discover: the two thousand years of the Church laid out as a timeline you move through by hand, divided into eleven ages from the Apostolic Age to the present. Thirty-eight events to begin, the councils and the schisms, the saints and the missions and the martyrs, each with its own page, its full account, and its sources shown in the open. Move by era, jump by century, search by name or year or place, and filter by category. Every event links into the saints, councils, and doctrine already in the app, and each saint and council page now points back to its place in history. It all works without an account, and on Android it works fully offline.

sections.heading: Honest about what is certain
sections.body: Church history holds firm dates and treasured traditions side by side, and Purify never pretends the second are the first. Every event wears a plain label, from Historically Attested to Traditional Account to Disputed, and says so wherever it matters. The facts, the sources, and the citations are free for everyone, always. A richer, cinematic way to experience the history, with artwork and gentle motion, is being prepared for Purify Plus; the history itself will never move behind it.

sections.heading: On this day, and where you left off
sections.body: Today has become a personal daily page. It greets you by the hour, names the rule that hour calls for, and remembers your rhythm of prayer. Beside it, a quiet thread of your own: the chapter you were reading, your place on the History timeline, the prayers you opened, your saved passages. When a firmly dated event falls on today, it appears here as On This Day in Orthodox History.

sections.heading: The library, redrawn
sections.body: Discover, the Bible, and the Today page now share one calm editorial hand instead of three. The Bible's canon reads as a single library rather than a wall of coloured tiles, and remembers the exact verse you left off at. Discover leads with what is worth returning to and shows the life of the day. The section marks throughout have been redrawn to suit what they open, an hourglass for history, a shield for the defense of the faith.

sections.heading: Signing in, mended
sections.body: Continue with Google stopped working for a spell, turned away at the door with an error that was ours to fix, not yours. It is mended. If you have only ever signed in with Google, that is the door to use; if you set a password in the early days, it still works, and Forgot password will always let you set a fresh one. The Google and Apple marks on the sign-in buttons are drawn properly now, too.

closing: This one took a while, and it was worth every hour. If a date looks wrong, a source looks thin, or an event you love is missing, tell me, this is a beginning and not an end. Write to me at lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email, and I pray for the people who send them.

title: Steadier on Android
intro: A repair patch, written with the Android beta testers in hand. You opened the app, you found the rough edges, and you wrote them down kindly. This is the answer to that: sign-in that finishes where it starts, a top of the screen that no longer hides its own buttons, and a handful of quiet fixes. Thank you for testing. Glory to God for patient hands.

sections.heading: Signing in, and out, the way it should
sections.body: Continue with Google now completes inside the app, with the native account picker, instead of sending you out to a separate browser and leaving you signed in everywhere but here. And signing out no longer ends on an error screen; it simply lets you go, quietly, back to the start.

sections.heading: Nothing hiding behind the clock
sections.body: On Android the very top of the screen used to slip up under the status bar, taking buttons with it. The welcome's Skip, the Cancel in Bible search, the app's own header: all of them now sit below the clock and the battery, where your thumb can actually reach them. The Android back button closes the search sheet instead of feeling stuck.

sections.heading: A few quiet repairs
sections.body: Long prayer titles read in full now, rather than trailing off mid-word. Turning on prayer reminders no longer stumbles. And the app finally wears its own icon, the three-bar cross, in your app drawer and on your home screen, in place of the placeholder it shipped with.

closing: Small as it is, every patch is offered with thanks for the people praying alongside this work. If something feels off, or there is a feature you wish existed, write to me at lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email.

title: A gentler welcome
intro: A small patch about first steps. New here? Purify now opens with a short, skippable welcome that helps you set your calendar and find a good place to begin. Everyone who has been here before is left exactly where they were. Glory to God for new faces.

sections.heading: A first-run welcome
sections.body: Open Purify for the first time and you are met with three quiet screens: a word about what this is, a chance to choose the calendar you keep, New or Old, and a gentle pointer toward a first step, depending on what draws you. It is entirely skippable, and it never shows again once you are in. If you have used Purify before, you will not see it at all.

sections.heading: Begin here
sections.body: After the welcome, the Today screen carries a single calm pointer toward that first step, the Gospel of John, the morning rule, the saints, or the day's reading, which you can follow or dismiss with a tap. No checklist, no streak, no score. Just one open door. Prayer is not a game to be won.

closing: Small as it is, every patch is offered with thanks for the people praying alongside this work. If something feels off, or there is a feature you wish existed, write to me at lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email.

title: A little tidying
intro: A small housekeeping patch. Nothing new to learn, just a few surfaces made calmer and easier to move through. Glory to God for the quiet weeks that let us polish what is already here.

sections.heading: The saints, sorted
sections.body: The saints index now lets you filter by kind, not only by century. Browse the Apostles, the Cappadocian Fathers, the Church Fathers, the Desert and monastic saints, the Fathers of the Councils, the Martyrs, the Wonderworkers, the Holy Women, and more. A saint can belong to several of these at once, and the counts on each filter update as you narrow down. Both the 'By kind' and 'By century' rows fold away with a tap when you want them out of the way. The Most Holy Theotokos remains pinned at the top, as the most perfect of the saints.

sections.heading: A lighter Today
sections.body: The cards on the mobile Today screen, the verse of the day, the saint, the fast, the readings, and the Pascha countdown, have been tightened up so more of the day fits on the screen at once without feeling cramped.

sections.heading: Home polish
sections.body: The four 'Why Purify' pillars now carry hand-drawn illustrations instead of plain glyphs, and the 'What we are made of' provenance cards have been trimmed to a single clear line each. Less to read, the same honesty about where every text comes from.

closing: Small as it is, every patch is offered with thanks for the people praying alongside this work. If something feels off, or there is a feature you wish existed, write to me at lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email.

title: Hello, faithful
intro:
Glory to Jesus Christ. This is the first public look at Purify, the Orthodox companion app I have been building. Everything you see is the work of one person; God willing, the team will grow. Thank you for being here at the beginning.

Purify is meant to be a single home for the Orthodox spiritual life: the Scriptures, the prayers, the saints, the seasons of the Church year, and a marketplace that supports those who carry the Faith. The free tier is broad and complete; the paid tier exists to keep the lights on, fund patristic commentary curation, and support priests through paid blessings.

sections.heading: The Orthodox Bible
sections.body:
The full Orthodox canon, all 77 books, end to end. Old Testament from Brenton's English Septuagint of 1851, including the deuterocanonical books that most modern English Bibles omit. New Testament from the King James Version. Both are public domain. Brenton in particular is the English form of the Greek Septuagint, the version of the Old Testament read by the Apostles themselves and still used by the Orthodox Church.

You can switch books from anywhere with a search-friendly dropdown. Arrow keys move between chapters. Books are grouped by their traditional sections: Pentateuch, Historical, Wisdom, Prophets, Gospels, Acts, Pauline Epistles, Catholic Epistles, Revelation. Twelve of the most-read books carry short Orthodox introductions; the rest will follow.

sections.heading: Patristic commentary
sections.body:
Brief commentary from the Fathers appears in a side rail next to the verses they wrote on. The current corpus includes Basil the Great, John Chrysostom, Augustine, Cyril of Alexandria, Jerome, Gregory of Nyssa, and Gregory the Theologian. The two Gregories and Basil, the three Cappadocians, are the heart of fourth-century Orthodox theology, and their voices will only grow louder in future patches.

Clicking a verse with commentary scrolls the rail to that verse. Clicking a commentary card expands the quote inline. Saint icons appear as the photos themselves where available, and as deterministic initials in colored circles where they are not yet uploaded.

sections.heading: Reader controls
sections.body: Cycle text size through four presets: Small, Medium, Large, X-Large. Swap between three font families: Serif, Display, Sans. Highlight verses with a single click on the toolbar, or highlight individual words by clicking, or stretch the highlight across as many words as you like with a drag. Add a personal note to any verse. Everything saves locally to your device for now; cloud sync arrives with accounts.

sections.heading: Learn to pray
sections.body: A six-lesson beginner path for anyone new to Orthodox prayer: what prayer is, the Sign of the Cross, the Jesus Prayer, the Trisagion, and a simple morning and evening rule. Each lesson is about five minutes, with the full text of the prayer and a short 'try this' application.

sections.heading: The rest of the app
sections.body: Pricing tier, account scaffolding, prayer campaigns, the Orthodox calendar, saints' works, the marketplace, and monastery directory are all real routes. They are currently stubs and waiting for the features that fill them in next. Mobile responsiveness, a PWA manifest, and the dark Hallow-style design are in across the whole app.

future.title: More patristic commentary
future.body: The Cappadocians have hundreds of pages of Bible commentary. So do Chrysostom, Maximus the Confessor, and John of Damascus. Careful ingestion from public-domain sources, mapped to specific verses, with brief modern summaries written for readers new to the Fathers.

future.title: The Orthodox calendar
future.body: Feasts, fasts, saints of the day, in both the New (Revised Julian) and Old (Julian) calendars, plus jurisdictional options for those who follow Antiochian, Greek, Russian, Serbian, or other traditional cycles.

future.title: NKJV and the Orthodox Study Bible
future.body: Licensing outreach is open to Thomas Nelson / HarperCollins Christian Publishing for the NKJV text and the published Orthodox Study Bible notes. Until they say yes, the Brenton + KJV public-domain edition is what we ship. The infrastructure to drop NKJV in is already built and waiting.

future.title: Daily readings
future.body: The lectionary, the appointed Gospel, Epistle, and Old Testament for each day of the Church year, pulled directly into the Bible reader so you can pray with the Church wherever you are.

future.title: Accounts and cloud sync
future.body: Optional sign-in so your highlights, notes, and prayer-plan progress travel with you across devices. Local-only is fine for now; nothing of yours leaves your device today.

future.title: Full prayer plans
future.body: Morning and evening rules from the standard prayer books, akathists, the canon to the Theotokos, Holy Week services, and seasonal plans for Great Lent and Pascha. Personal plan-building for the paid tier.

future.title: The Marketplace
future.body: Verified monastery storefronts, independent iconographers, prayer rope makers, Orthodox booksellers, and paid blessings that fund priests directly. Stripe Connect for sellers and donations.

future.title: Audio
future.body: Reading the Scriptures aloud, the akathists, the prayer rules, and the lives of saints, so you can pray while walking or driving.

future.title: Native mobile apps
future.body: iOS and Android, with offline reading of the Bible, prayer book, and lives of saints. The web app is the foundation; the native shells follow once the web feels right.

closing:
This is a beta. Things will break. The web font sometimes flashes before swapping to your preferred size. Highlights live in your browser, not in the cloud, until accounts ship. Some chapters do not yet have patristic commentary; those that do are the ones the Fathers wrote on most.

I am building this in the evenings while running other work. If something is wrong, or there is a feature you wish existed, please write to me at lifeistheosis@gmail.com. I read every email.

May the Lord bless this small offering.
